articles.title: Entenda caso da servidora que deve ter aposentadoria aumentada | G1
articles.standfirst: Servidora foi aprovada em concurso público para o cargo de auxiliar de serviços gerais, mas contribuiu como base no salário de fiscal de tributos. A Justiça determinou a revisão do valor.
articles.summary: Servidora foi aprovada em concurso público para o cargo de auxiliar de serviços gerais, mas contribuiu como base no salário de fiscal de tributos. A Justiça determinou a revisão do
articles.body:
Instituto de Previdência de Aparecida (AparecidaPrev), em Goiás — Foto: Prefeitura de Aparecida de Goiânia/ Reprodução

A transposição irregular do cargo e a contribuição da aposentada que deve ter o benefício elevado de R$ 1,9 mil para R$ 8,9 mil , são os pontos principais desse conflito. A Justiça reconheceu o direito da contribuinte ao novo valor, que deve ser calculado com base nas contribuições feitas por ela ao longo da carreira (entenda o conflito abaixo) . O Instituto de Previdência de Aparecida (AparecidaPrev) vai recorrer da decisão.

Em nota enviada ao g1 , o AparecidaPrev disse que "houve transposição irregular de cargo e que, por isso, a aposentadoria deve considerar o cargo de origem, de serviços gerais, e não o de fiscal de tributos" (leia a nota na íntegra ao fim do texto) .

A aposentada entrou no serviço público em 1990, no cargo de auxiliar de serviços gerais, mas exerceu a função de fiscal de tributos por 28 anos, segundo a sentença. O AparecidaPrev alega que houve transposição irregular do cargo , ou seja, exercendo uma função diferente daquela para a qual foi aprovada em concurso público .

Entretanto, a defesa, representada por Eurípedes Souza, alegou que durante quase três décadas a servidora contribuiu para a Previdência com um valor baseado na remuneração deste último cargo, que foi usada para calcular sua aposentadoria. Para o advogado, não seria razoável o poder público receber essas contribuições e desconsiderá-las no momento da aposentadoria.

Na sentença, o juiz Roberto Neiva Borges reconheceu que o instituto arrecadou as contribuições calculadas com base no salário que a servidora recebia como fiscal de tributos durante 28 anos, e não sobre o salário de auxiliar de serviços gerais, seu cargo original.

"Por 28 anos, a Administração Pública se beneficiou da força de trabalho da autora em função de maior complexidade e, durante todo esse período, o ente previdenciário arrecadou contribuições calculadas sobre a remuneração correspondente a essa função, sem qualquer oposição", diz o texto.

O magistrado afirmou que a imposição de um regime que resulta em benefício inferior ao cálculo pela média contributiva, viola o princípio do direito ao melhor benefício. Disse ainda que o regime de previdência social, embora solidário, possui caráter eminentemente contributivo .

"A desproporção entre as contribuições vertidas (calculadas sobre R$ 8.966,14) e o benefício concedido (R$ 1.903,22) configura enriquecimento sem causa do ente público, vedado pelo ordenamento jurídico", explicou.

Diante disso, o juiz reconheceu o direito da aposentada de calcular o benefício com base na média aritmética de 80% das suas maiores contribuições e condenou a AparecidaPrev a revisar o benefício de aposentadoria, fixando o valor de R$8.966,14 .

Além disso, em decisão de primeira instância, a Justiça condenou o instituto ao pagamento das diferenças de valores desde a data em que o benefício começou a ser pago, em 2022. O valor deverá ser pago corrigido pelo INPC, índice oficial que mede a inflação de famílias com renda mensal de 1 a 5 salários mínimos, acrescido de juros.

O AparecidaPrev informa que a servidora foi aprovada em concurso público para o cargo de serviços gerais, embora tenha exercido atividades de fiscal de tributos. O Instituto entende que houve transposição irregular de cargo e que, por isso, a aposentadoria deve considerar o cargo de origem, de serviços gerais, e não o de fiscal de tributos.

Como a sentença de primeira instância foi proferida em 14 de setembro de 2026 e o prazo recursal ainda está em curso, o AparecidaPrev apresentará recurso contra a decisão.

articles.title: Após ação do MP, Campinas inclui famílias de indígenas venezuelanos no programa de auxílio-moradia  | G1
articles.standfirst: Comunidade formada por 85 pessoas da etnia Warao vive no local, no Jardim Nova Esperança, há dois anos; benefício deve começar a ser pago em outubro.
articles.summary: Comunidade formada por 85 pessoas da etnia Warao vive no local, no Jardim Nova Esperança, há dois anos; benefício deve começar a ser pago em outubro.
articles.body:
Imóvel usado por 26 famílias indígenas venezuelanas em Campinas (SP), há dois anos, apresenta péssimas condições e motivou ação do Ministério Público; prefeitura apresentou plano de ação — Foto: Fernando Evans/g1

A situação de 26 famílias indígenas venezuelanas da etnia Warao que vivem em Campinas (SP) levou o Ministério Público de São Paulo (MP-SP) a acionar a Justiça após apontar condições precárias de moradia em um imóvel usado pela comunidade há dois anos .

Em reunião realizada na segunda-feira (21), representantes da prefeitura apresentaram um plano de ação para o atendimento dos 85 migrantes que residem no local.

A medida atende determinação do juiz responsável pelo caso, que reconheceu a vulnerabilidade da comunidade e havia determinado que o município apresentasse medidas concretas para enfrentar o problema.

Segundo a promotora Cristiane Hillal, houve avanço com a apresentação do plano que prevê a inclusão das famílias no programa municipal de auxílio-moradia . Atualmente, o benefício oferece pagamento de R$ 605,00 por mês, por 12 meses , podendo ser reavaliado ao final do período.

"O benefício começa a ser pago em 13 de outubro. A partir dessa data, elas terão prazo para buscar um novo local para morar", informou a administração.

Agora, a expectativa da promotoria está voltada à análise sobre as condições de um imóvel que poderá receber as famílias, alternativa considerada fundamental para a efetiva saída dos indígenas do local onde vivem atualmente.

O g1 foi até o imóvel localizado no Jardim Nova Esperança, nesta quarta-feira (23), mas os Waraos, temendo algum reflexo no avanço das negociações judiciais, não permitiram a entrada da equipe.

Atualmente, a comunidade gasta entre R$ 5,5 mil e R$ 6 mil por mês com a moradia (entre aluguel, água e luz), mas a infraestrutura, segundo a ação civil pública, é precária.

A renda do grupo vem principalmente da produção e venda de artesanatos pelas mulheres, e pelo trabalho de parte dos homens adultos da etnia - alguns atuam em empresas terceirizadas de limpeza, por exemplo.

O caso também é acompanhado pelo Núcleo Especializado de Promoção da Igualdade Racial e de Defesa dos Povos e Comunidades Tradicionais (NUPIR), da Defensoria Pública do Estado.

Segundo o órgão, o acompanhamento da comunidade Warao começou em março de 2026, após solicitação da 24ª Promotoria de Justiça de Campinas para a realização de uma visita conjunta às famílias indígenas venezuelanas.

A vistoria ocorreu em 7 de maio e permitiu mapear as principais demandas da comunidade, entre elas o acesso à moradia.

Após o ajuizamento da ação civil pública pelo Ministério Público, o NUPIR manteve o acompanhamento do caso e participou de reuniões com os órgãos públicos envolvidos na busca por soluções.

Em 14 de setembro, representantes da Defensoria voltaram a visitar a comunidade para verificar demandas ainda pendentes.

"Desde o primeiro encontro, os Warao haviam relatado dificuldades relacionadas ao acesso à educação, ao trabalho, ao transporte e à saúde, questões que, naquele momento, estavam sendo inicialmente tratadas pelo poder público municipal", informou a Defensoria.

Em nota, a prefeitura de Campinas informou que além da inclusão das famílias no programa de auxílio-moradia, já adotou ações de inclusão e atualização dos Warao no Cadastro Único e aos programas de transferência de renda do governo federal, bem como encaminhamentos à rede de saúde pública, entrega de itens básicos e oferta de apoio alimentar.

"A Prefeitura mantém ainda articulação com o Alto Comissariado das Nações Unidas para Refugiados (Acnur), inclusive para capacitação das equipes municipais sobre as especificidades culturais do povo Warao", destaca.

Sobre as famílias indígenas venezuelanas da etnia Warao que vivem em Campinas, a Prefeitura informa que:

"Apresentou à Justiça, nos autos do processo, o plano de atendimento realizado com essa população.

As famílias têm acesso aos programas sociais disponíveis no município e estão contempladas no Programa Auxílio-Moradia. O benefício começa a ser pago em 13 de outubro. A partir dessa data, elas terão prazo para buscar um novo local para morar.

A Secretaria de Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social mantém o acompanhamento das famílias, em articulação com a rede intersetorial de atendimento. Desde 2025, elas são acompanhadas no Jardim Nova Esperança pelo Serviço de Referência ao Imigrante, Refugiado e Apátrida e pelo Serviço de Abordagem Social.

Entre as ações realizadas estão a inclusão e atualização no Cadastro Único; o acesso a programas de transferência de renda (todas as famílias acompanhadas pelo Serviço de Abordagem Social estão inseridas no Programa Bolsa Família); encaminhamentos para a rede municipal de saúde; acompanhamento da frequência e da vida escolar de crianças e adolescentes; entrega de itens básicos, como colchões, cobertores e kits de higiene; e a oferta de apoio alimentar.

Neste momento, a Secretaria de Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social mantém interlocução com a Secretaria Nacional de Assistência Social (SNAS/MDS), do Governo Federal, para apoio técnico e financeiro à questão.

Também estão em andamento tratativas para uma reunião entre representantes de Campinas, do Governo do Estado de São Paulo e do Governo Federal, com o objetivo de discutir estratégias de atuação conjunta.

A Prefeitura mantém ainda articulação com o Alto Comissariado das Nações Unidas para Refugiados (Acnur), inclusive para capacitação das equipes municipais sobre as especificidades culturais do povo Warao.

A Administração Municipal seguirá adotando as medidas necessárias para o acompanhamento das famílias, em conformidade com a legislação."

articles.title: Desabamento no Morro do Cantagalo: casas vizinhas são interditadas | G1
articles.standfirst: A Defesa Civil Municipal decidiu esvaziar imóveis vizinhos preventivamente, por conta da proximidade com os escombros.
articles.summary: O desabamento no Morro do Cantagalo levou à interdição de sete imóveis pela Defesa Civil após o recorde de chuvas no Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:
Pelo menos 7 imóveis foram interditados após o desabamento de um prédio no Morro do Cantagalo , na Zona Sul do Rio de Janeiro , no fim da noite desta quarta-feira (23).

A Defesa Civil Municipal decidiu esvaziar casas vizinhas preventivamente , por conta da proximidade com os escombros, até que a remoção do entulho seja feita pela Secretaria Municipal de Conservação.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia prazo para a liberação das residências .

O Globocop sobrevoou o local do desabamento. Era possível ver um grande volume de destroços e árvores arrastadas.

Local onde prédio desabou no Morro do Cantagalo, na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Reprodução

Local onde prédio desabou no Morro do Cantagalo, na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: Reprodução / TV Globo

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros e o prefeito Eduardo Cavaliere (PSD), ninguém ficou ferido . O prédio ficava na Rua Saint Roman 15, no acesso à comunidade do Pavão-Pavãozinho, entre os bairros de Copacabana e Ipanema.

O imóvel estava em processo de demolição, pois se tratava de uma obra irregular denunciada pelos próprios moradores da região, informou Cavaliere pelas redes sociais. O imóvel estava interditado desde o início do mês pela Defesa Civil.

Nas redes sociais, Cavaliere alertou para os riscos que a cidade do Rio de Janeiro enfrenta nessa época de chuvas. “Essas construções ilegais que vão se acumulando, ganhando pavimento, verticalizando, coloca a vida, principalmente das pessoas que vivem aqui, em risco”, disse o prefeito.

Vídeos compartilhados nas redes sociais registraram o momento em que a construção desaba. As imagens mostram uma nuvem de poeira tomando conta da área e moradores deixando o local às pressas. (Veja acima)

Também é possível ver uma pilha de escombros ocupando parte da via ao lado de outras construções da comunidade.

Prédio desaba no Morro do Cantagalo, no Rio de Janeiro. — Foto: Reprodução / Redes Sociais

Equipes de resgate avaliam destruição após prédio desabar no Morro do Cantagalo. — Foto: Ricardo Guimarães / TV Globo

A cidade do Rio de Janeiro registrou o mês de setembro mais chuvoso dos últimos 29 anos antes mesmo do fim do período. O recorde foi alcançado nesta quarta, de acordo com o Sistema Alerta Rio, serviço meteorológico da Prefeitura do Rio.

Até as 8h45 de quarta, a capital fluminense havia acumulado 163,2 mm de chuva ao longo do mês . O volume supera os 157,7 mm registrados em setembro de 2005 , que, até então, era o maior índice desde o início da série histórica do Alerta Rio.

O terceiro maior acumulado para setembro foi registrado em 2022, quando choveu 144,7 mm .

Em quase todas as regiões da cidade, o volume de chuva já ultrapassou os 100 mm. Em alguns pontos, o acumulado supera o dobro da média climatológica para o mês.

articles.title: Dr. Luisinho disputa governo do Acre com proposta de polo industrial | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresário de 51 anos disputa o Executivo Estadual pela primeira vez em chapa pura. Candidato defende criação de faculdade técnica e otimização do orçamento bilionário do estado.
articles.summary: Empresário de 51 anos disputa o Executivo Estadual pela primeira vez em chapa pura. Candidato defende criação de faculdade técnica e otimização do orçamento bilionário do estado.
articles.body:
O candidato Dr. Luisinho, do partido Agir, disputa pela primeira vez o Governo do Acre nas eleições de 2026. Aos 51 anos, o acreano é bacharel em Direito e Teologia, contador e jornalista, e esta é a sua primeira disputa ao Executivo do Acre.

Com atuação no setor financeiro e empresarial desde 2004, atualmente preside o conselho de administração de um banco de crédito e desenvolvimento, além do Instituto Fundo Solidário para a Amazônia.

Com uma plataforma voltada ao desenvolvimento econômico e ao fortalecimento da infraestrutura, o candidato propõe atrair indústrias e implementar medidas definitivas contra desastres naturais no estado. Sua única experiência eleitoral anterior ocorreu em 2020, quando concorreu ao cargo de vereador em Manaus (AM).

A principal bandeira de Dr. Luisinho é a geração de emprego e renda por meio do incentivo à industrialização. O plano de governo do candidato elenca 12 metas prioritárias para a economia acreana, com destaque para a criação de um distrito industrial de alta capacidade tecnológica.

Para viabilizar o projeto, o candidato propõe a criação da Faculdade de Estado de Audopia (Fepe), uma instituição de ensino voltada exclusivamente para a qualificação técnica dos trabalhadores que irão atuar nas novas indústrias do estado.

"A Faculdade de Estado de Audopia vai preparar essa mão de obra para o Distrito Industrial e criar os empregos do futuro. Nós temos o plano anti enchente do Estado do Acre, porque todos os anos a população do Estado do Acre sofre dos problemas de desastre naturais. Por que não resolver? Nós temos como resolver, porque dinheiro o Estado tem", disse em entrevista à Rede Amazônica Acre.

Dr. Luisinho (Agir) apresenta propostas caso seja eleito governador do Acre — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Amazônica

Diante das recorrentes cheias que afetam as cidades acreanas, Dr. Luisinho defende a execução de um plano preventivo de engenharia e contesta a falta de investimentos na área, apontando que o estado dispõe de recursos financeiros suficientes para solucionar o problema.

Na área de serviços públicos, Dr. Luisinho destaca que sua gestão priorizará canais diretos de diálogo com a comunidade para ouvir os moradores, mapear as demandas locais e definir as prioridades de investimento do governo.

"Nós temos hoje um orçamento de quase R$ 13,8 bilhões que podem ser distribuídos em várias áreas do Estado. E por que não se fazem? Porque os nossos políticos não estão muito preocupados em desenvolver o nosso Estado", afirmou o candidato.

Dr. Luisinho (Agir) é candidato ao governo do Acre pela primeira vez — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Amazônica

A Rede Amazônica definiu uma série de entrevistas ao vivo com os candidatos mais bem colocados na primeira pesquisa Quaest contratada e divulgada pela emissora. Além de estar entre os cinco primeiros, o candidato precisava atingir pelo menos 5% das intenções de voto na pesquisa estimulada.

As entrevistas na TV ocorreram entre os dias 14 a 17 de setembro, durante o Jornal do Acre 1ª Edição. Cada candidato teve 25 minutos para responder às perguntas, incluindo as considerações finais.

Segunda-feira (14): Tião Bocalom (PL) - não compareceu

Quarta-feira (16): Alan Rick (Republicanos) - confira o balanço completo

Quinta-feira (17): Mailza Assis (PP) - confira o balanço completo

Candidatos ao governo do Acre nas eleições de 2026 — Foto: Reprodução

Os demais candidatos que não ficaram entre os primeiros colocados ou não atingiram 5% das intenções de voto na pesquisa tiveram espaço em reportagens gravadas de dois minutos.

articles.body: HYDERABAD: A 55-year-old SI of Bhadradri Kothagudem district who was on Ganesh idol immersion bandobust duties in Hyderabad died after he was hit by a two-wheeler on Tank Bund. Police teams are verifying the CCTV footage from nearby areas to identify the accused.The victim, K Venkanna, was an SI of Kothagudem II Town PS. He was among the 10 cops of Kothagudem II Town PS deployed in Hyderabad for Ganesh idol immersion security duties. At around 1.50 am on Wednesday, when Venkanna, along with another cop, was crossing Tank Bund road, a two-wheeler hit him.Venkanna, who sustained injuries to his right hand and leg, was shifted from the spot in a police vehicle to a private hospital in Lakdikapul. According to Saifabad police, doctors who examined him thought he had only sustained injuries to his hand and leg and gave first aid.According to Kothagudem police, Venkanna was a native of Kistapuram village in Thorrur mandal of Mahabubabad. “His family and friends did not think it was a head injury. They shifted him to a private hospital in Hanamkonda, closer to his native place in the afternoon. While undergoing treatment, his condition suddenly became critical due to internal head injury and he succumbed on Wednesday night,” Kothagudem II Town SI K Raja Sekhar said.Meanwhile, Saifabad police said that they are trying to identify and arrest the accused. “We have registered a case on Wednesday morning and after the death, the section has been altered to fatal road accident. articles.title: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro': CJP to take up issue of EC reforms as CEC Gyanesh Kumar faces flak
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which has been campaigning on issues including school infrastructure and tribal education, has shifted its
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which has been campaigning on issues including school infrastructure and tribal education, has shifted its focus to electoral reforms, saying its efforts on other problems would have little impact if people's right to vote was compromised.Taking a swipe at chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a popular meme stating that “it’s over.”According to news agency PTI, Dipke indicated that the organisation would take up reforms in the Election Commission after differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls came into the open on Wednesday."Election Commission Thik Karo! Important PC tomorrow in Delhi. Gyanesh, it's done bro," Dipke said on X.The CJP cancelled programmes scheduled for Thursday and said its leadership would hold a press conference in Delhi at noon on what it called the "Hijacking of India's Democracy".‘Nothing is going to work’CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that the Election Commission was "stealing our votes"."Nothing is going to work because the Election Commission of India is compromised," Das said.In a video statement, Das said the organisation could continue campaigning on schools, unemployment, infrastructure and examination irregularities, but such efforts would ultimately serve little purpose if people were unable to exercise their right to vote and change the system through elections."We can do as many School Theek Karos, we can do as many Adivasi School Theek Karos... but nothing is going to help if our final tool that we can use to change our system, the right to vote, is stolen from us," Das said.He said elections were the "fundamental tool to bring change" and questioned how anything could change if elections were "stolen away" from the younger generation and others."The fundamental tool to bring change is elections," Das said, adding that if elections were "stolen away" from the younger generation and others, "then how is anything going to change?"The organisation said it was therefore seeking greater attention to the functioning of the poll panel and protection of the right to vote.The CJP's announcement came after Indian Express reported on Wednesday that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders of the Election Commission.The objections reportedly included decisions on the addition, deletion and restoration of voters, as well as changes to the voter registration process during the SIR of electoral rolls.The opposition has demanded that the SIR be scrapped and has called for the impeachment and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In the wake of the report, EC officials said the two commissioners had flagged decisions taken during the electoral roll cleanup and handling of the voter database in various states.EC sources, however, maintained that all decisions of the Election Commission of India, including SIR, have been unanimous and taken with the approval of both the Election articles.title: Inside China’s nuclear buildup: New activity spotted across 7 sites, claims report
articles.summary: China is expanding infrastructure linked to its nuclear weapons programme at multiple sites across the country, with new construction and upgrades
articles.body: China is expanding infrastructure linked to its nuclear weapons programme at multiple sites across the country, with new construction and upgrades reported at facilities associated with nuclear research, testing and weapons production.According to Telegraph investigation, based on satellite imagery and expert analysis, identified activity at seven sites, including Pingtong, Zitong, Lop Nur, Jiuquan, Mianyang, Jinta and Guangyuan.The reported developments span different parts of China's nuclear weapons infrastructure, indicating a broader expansion beyond missile deployment alone.The Federation of American Scientists, in its 2026 Nuclear Notebook, estimates that China has about 620 nuclear warheads, with additional warheads being produced for future delivery systems. FAS said China has continued developing new ICBM silo fields, additional DF-5 silos, new ICBM variants and advanced strategic delivery systems.China's nuclear modernisation also extends beyond land-based missiles. According to FAS, Beijing is expanding its fleet of nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines, fitting Type 094 submarines with longer-range JL-3 missiles and developing the next-generation Type 096 submarine.China has also assigned a nuclear mission to some H-6 bombers equipped with an air-launched ballistic missile that may have nuclear capability.The report comes as Chinese President Xi Jinping meets US President Donald Trump in Washington. In a written statement after his arrival, Xi said China and the US should be “partners, not rivals” and called for a stable relationship centred on cooperation, measured competition and manageable differencesChina's nuclear policyDespite the expansion, Beijing continues to publicly describe its nuclear posture as defensive.In its 2026 submission to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty review process, China said it follows a nuclear strategy of self-defence, maintains a policy of no first use of nuclear weapons and keeps its nuclear strength at the minimum level required for national security.China foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said in April that China's nuclear policy is based on self-defence and no first use, while Beijing would not participate in a nuclear arms race with any country.In May, Chinese arms-control official Sun Xiaobo said the country's no-first-use policy and its approach of maintaining nuclear capabilities at the minimum level required for national security would not change.The expansion of China's nuclear infrastructure has nevertheless prompted debate among US and independent analysts over how the growing size and diversity of its arsenal could affect its nuclear posture.The Federation of American Scientists has said there is little evidence that Beijing has formally abandoned its no-first-use policy, while noting that China's expanding force is making its nuclear capabilities increasingly sophisticated and survivable.

articles.title: 'Inappropriate to ask': Years before Sahil Wakode's death, IIT-Bombay professor warned students against caste discrimination
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A 2024 email sent by IIT Bombay professor Suryanarayana Doolla, who was then the institute’s Dean of Student Affairs, has resurfaced amid
articles.body: MUMBAI: A 2024 email sent by IIT Bombay professor Suryanarayana Doolla, who was then the institute’s Dean of Student Affairs, has resurfaced amid allegations of caste discrimination made by the family of student Sahil Wakode, who died by suicide last week.In the email, prof Doolla cautioned students against asking fellow students about their admission categories, JEE (Advanced) ranks or GATE scores, saying such questions could reveal their caste or whether they belonged to a reserved category.The email said IIT Bombay aimed to promote an inclusive campus where students interacted with each other irrespective of caste, religion or socio-economic status."IIT Bombay considers it inappropriate to ask a fellow student what birth/admission category they belong to: asking this could lead to conscious or subconscious bias.It is equally inappropriate for any person (students/staff/faculty-members) to ask other students about their JEE (Advanced) ranks/GATE-scores, or any other information that may reveal the caste or other related aspects. While the person asking the question may feel it is innocent, and it may be driven purely by curiosity, asking the question can often have an adverse impact on the other student. Asking could appear like an attempt to find the caste, and may set the stage for discrimination."The message also urged students to build friendships around common interests such as their department, sports, music, films, schools, colleges, villages, cities and hobbies."It is prohibited to exchange/forward any messages, including jokes, that are abusive, hateful, casteist, sexist, exhibit bigotry e.g. based on - religion or sexual orientation, can be construed as harassment or bullying."The email said the prohibition applied to messages shared on WhatsApp, Facebook and email, as well as interactions in person, and warned that violations could lead to severe punishment.The email was circulated during prof Doolla’s tenure as dean. IIT Bombay had also circulated its anti-discrimination guidelines twice during his tenure.An ApologyThe institue on Thursday issued a formal apology over statements made in an earlier communication about the circumstances surrounding the death of student Sahil Ravindra Wakode.Re-sharing a statement originally published on X on September 21, IIT Bombay said it had been premature to release or characterise details about the events leading up to the incident before formal inquiries were completed.“Sharing the earlier post of 21st Sept 2026 again: We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil. The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities,” the post read.The institute said the circumstances surrounding Wakode's death remained under investigation by legal and law enforcement agencies.“In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process,” IIT Bombay stated in the post on X.Sahil Wakode’s deathProf Doolla had allegedly caught Wakode using a mobile phone inside an examination hall on September 18. Hours later, the 20-year-old second-year student was found dead in his hostel room.Wakode’s parents have alleged that their son had complained of being subjected to casteist remarks a few days before his death. The allegations have led to protests by students on the IIT Bombay campus.The city crime branch is investigating a case of alleged abetment to suicide in connection with Wakode’s death.Police have collected CCTV footage showing Wakode’s movements during the examination in which he was allegedly caught copying.According to investigators, footage from September 18 shows Wakode inside the examination hall between about 12.30pm and 12.45pm, as the semester examination was nearing its end.The footage allegedly shows him bending down and looking at a mobile phone kept in his pocket. Police are also examining an allegation that he was using ChatGPT to answer questions during the examination.The footage then shows the invigilator noticing Wakode’s movements and approaching him. The invigilator is seen taking his answer sheet and asking him to leave the examination hall.Wakode is then seen getting up, collecting his belongings and preparing to leave. articles.title: ​At 90, former paratrooper Ian Winship runs 10K in about an hour with daughter and grandson, setting a world-best time for his age
articles.summary: Ian Winship, a 90-year-old runner from North Lanarkshire, has completed a 10-kilometre race in about 1 hour, 4 minutes and 37 seconds, setting what is
articles.body: Ian Winship, a 90-year-old runner from North Lanarkshire, has completed a 10-kilometre race in about 1 hour, 4 minutes and 37 seconds, setting what is believed to be a world-best time for his age group. On 13 September, the former paratrooper completed the Cumbernauld 10K run. "I stood greetin'," the former paratrooper told the BBC, his disbelief still evident.It's easy to understand why. Winship wasn't chasing records when he started that morning. He was doing what he does most days: running. The world-best time in the M90 category came out of the blue. “It's just unbelievable. Cumbernauld might be famous now because of me.”Scottish Athletics confirmed the achievement is considered a ‘world best’ rather than a ‘world record’, as non-professional road races lack the precision required for official ratification. But there are simply no reports of anyone older achieving a faster time.Age, just a numberIan Winship, who hails from Cumberland, revealed the secret behind the record. He gets up each morning, fetches his paper, gets his coffee, and walks. Not around the block, but for miles. Most days, he hits 20,000 steps. Long stretches through Cumbernauld are a regimen he religiously follows to keep himself fit.Winship understands what most people don’t. “I've got a purpose, I want to stay alive. If I sit in the house I'll vegetate. I must meet people.” So he walks and continues to share ties with the community. It’s the perspective of someone who spent his younger years as a paratrooper, jumping into Egypt near Port Said during the Suez Crisis in 1956, and later became a steeplejack. Motion was always the job. Now it's the medicine.For him, what really works is consistency. He does not have a fancy training plan or gym membership. But every morning he wakes up and gets moving. His next challenge is to ‘live to 100’.When Winship completed the race, he was a little ‘wobbly’, so the paramedics offered him a wheelchair. But the 90-year-old turned it down immediately.3 generations in motionWinship had the best company in the race. The nonagenarian ran this race alongside his daughter, Fiona Fleming, and grandson Kyle Fleming, 26, who came third. It wasn't their first time making the race a family affair at Cumbernauld. But the grandfather's performance still caught them off guard.Kyle is proud of his grandpa. “He gets up every morning, goes to get his paper, goes to get his coffee. He does 20,000 steps a day. It's incredible,” he told the broadcaster."I run because it keeps me sane, keeps me fit and it keeps me out of trouble,” Winship always told his family.For Kyle, watching his grandpa was inspiration enough. "That's always stuck with me. Every time I see him running, that's what I think about. He lost his wife years ago, and I think it just keeps him going."Meanwhile, Scottish Athletics said Winship's achievement is considered a ‘world best’ in the M90 category. A spokesperson for the body said they were "delighted to hear of Ian's great run". "Athletics can be for life if that's what you want and performances like this one by Ian at 90 really are inspirational."Kenneth Duffy, provost of North Lanarkshire, called him ‘a hero’. "My huge congratulations to Ian on his outstanding achievement at this year's Cumbernauld 10K event. What a hero he is! I'm sure everyone will be inspired by his determination, commitment and enthusiasm. To complete a 10K at 90 years of age is a remarkable accomplishment, let alone complete it in such an impressive time."Geraldine Woods, convener of communities at the council, also lauded Winship’s achievement. "Ian's performance at this year's event, along with his dedication and positive attitude, is an inspiration to people of all ages."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: An Alabama couple bought 21 acres in Jackson Hole in the 1990s; decades later, their family retreat is asking $40 million
articles.summary: An Alabama couple who bought a 21-acre property in Jackson Hole in the 1990s has spent decades turning it into a family retreat with a Western-style
articles.body: An Alabama couple who bought a 21-acre property in Jackson Hole in the 1990s has spent decades turning it into a family retreat with a Western-style lodge, guest cottage and creek and riverfront grounds. Investor Jon Rotenstreich and his wife, Susan, initially lived in the two-bedroom guest cottage while renovating and expanding the main house to about 5,900 square feet. The compound also includes a 1,730-square-foot barn, an art studio, a teepee and a section of the Snake River. Now, after years of summers, holidays and family visits, the Rotenstreichs are listing the property for $40 million.How did the Rotenstreichs expand their Jackson Hole retreatAfter purchasing the property, the Rotenstreichs initially lived in the two-bedroom guest cottage while renovating the main house. According to The Wall Street Journal, they expanded the main house to about 5,900 square feet. Details were added throughout the home, including a main staircase with a handrail made by a woodworker who measured Susan’s hand to customise the size of the grip.The property also includes a garage with an art studio, where Susan, a former jewellery designer trained as an energy healer, liked to paint. A 1,730-square-foot barn contains a workshop, while a teepee is also located on the grounds. The couple’s grandchildren have slept in the teepee, and the family has used the area for campfires, songs and roasting marshmallows and s’mores.What natural features and Western-style interiors define the Jackson Hole retreatThe Jackson Hole compound includes both the creek and a section of the Snake River. A small island in the middle of the Snake River provides habitat for moose, elk and deer. Susan Rotenstreich said the family can snowshoe there during winter. The property also has a kitchen garden outside the main house, enclosed by a fence made from woven willow branches.The interiors were also developed in a Western style, with the Rotenstreichs using local craftsmen during the renovation. A local blacksmith handmade all of the fireplace tools, while a carpenter made furniture and decorative birch cabinets. The guest cottage includes a bookcase made from half of an old canoe, and the furniture in the home is included in the asking price.Why are the Rotenstreichs selling their $40 million Jackson Hole propertyThe Rotenstreichs are now selling the Jackson Hole property for $40 million. The compound includes a six-bedroom main house and a two-bedroom guest cottage. The couple declined to disclose how much they originally paid for the property, with the Journal noting that Wyoming is a nondisclosure state.The couple said they are selling because they feel it is time to downsize, although they still plan to visit Jackson Hole. The property is in the Ely Springs subdivision near Jackson. Listing agent Latham Jenkins of Live Water Properties told the Journal that real-estate values in the area have risen sharply since COVID and said the top end of the market continues to see demand.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Election Commission to decide at the earliest which of the two rival factions of the All India Trinamool Congress will get the party's name and symbol.Hearing a plea filed by Mamata Banerjee, the top court asked the poll panel to inform it by Monday when it expected to take a final decision on the dispute.The Supreme Court also referred to the Shiv Sena factional dispute and said the row between the two AITC factions should be decided expeditiously.The development comes days after the Election Commission temporarily allotted Mamata Banerjee's faction the name "Mamata All India Trinamool Congress" and the "football player" symbol.The rival faction was allotted the name "Democratic Trinamool Congress" and the "envelope" symbol.Earlier, in an interim order, the poll panel froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and its "flowers and grass" symbol after recognising a factional dispute within the party. articles.title: 'Die then, we won't stop': Passengers begged driver to pull over before Noida bus caught fire; 9 dead
articles.summary: NOIDA: Nine passengers were killed after a bus travelling from Delhi to Mahoba in Uttar Pradesh caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Greater Noida late
articles.body: NOIDA: Nine passengers were killed after a bus travelling from Delhi to Mahoba in Uttar Pradesh caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Greater Noida late Wednesday night, with an FIR alleging that the driver and conductor ignored repeated warnings from passengers about a burning smell and refused to stop the vehicle.Passengers repeatedly asked the driver to pull over after noticing the smell, but the driver and conductor allegedly told them, "If you want to die, then die; we won't stop the bus," according to the FIR registered on the complaint of a passenger, news agency PTI reported.The FIR was registered at Jewar police station on the complaint of Suneel Kumar, a resident of Hamirpur district. Kumar said he boarded the Raj Kalpana Travels bus from Delhi's Kashmere Gate around 9pm on Wednesday.About 30-35 passengers were on board, according to his complaint.Passengers noticed burning smellKumar said the bus reached the 33-km mark on the Yamuna Expressway at around 11.30pm when passengers noticed a burning smell coming from the driver's cabin.The driver allegedly dismissed it as a common smell in the bus and did not stop to check the vehicle, the complaint said.Kumar further alleged that the driver and conductor continued smoking bidis and cigarettes in the cabin before flames suddenly erupted near the driver's seat.Passengers raised an alarm and again asked the driver to stop, but the two allegedly refused, according to the complaint.By the time the bus stopped, the fire had spread through the vehicle and smoke had filled the passenger compartment, Kumar said.He and several other passengers managed to jump out of the bus, while some passengers remained trapped inside.Several passengers suffered burns and were taken to Kailash Hospital in Jewar for treatment. Kumar said he was later informed at the hospital that nine people had been declared dead.Police said the nine passengers died from burns and suffocation.Driver, conductor detainedThe complaint accused the driver and conductor of "deliberate, gross negligence, rashness and reckless disregard" for passenger safety.It also alleged that passengers' bags, luggage and mobile phones were destroyed in the fire, including belongings kept in the luggage compartment and on the roof of the bus.Police said the driver and conductor have been detained and that further investigation is underway.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news. articles.title: How China helped arm Iran before Trump rolled out the red carpet for Xi
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump hosted a grand welcome for Chinese president Xi Jinping but in the background of this fanfare, an investigation by the Wall
articles.body: US president Donald Trump hosted a grand welcome for Chinese president Xi Jinping but in the background of this fanfare, an investigation by the Wall Street Journal has shown how China has been supporting Iran militarily in its war against the US.When the US and Iran agreed to a temporary truce this summer, China was quick to highlight its diplomatic role.Beijing said its foreign ministry had made dozens of calls to help ease tensions, while Xi Jinping had personally offered suggestions aimed at ending the conflict.But on the very day the truce was signed, a Chinese aircraft landed in Tehran carrying electronics for Iran’s ministry of defense. According to Iranian customs records analysed by WSJ, some of the components could be used in drone systems and missile guidance equipment.This shipment was also not an isolated incident, as WSJ found records of around 1,300 shipments of dual-use components from China to Iran’s defence ministry through the end of June. Two days after the truce-day delivery, more than a dozen additional shipments arrived carrying parts worth over $6 million that could be used in drones.With Xi currently in Washington for talks with Trump, China's relationship with Iran has emerged as an uncomfortable issue sitting beneath the official summit agenda of trade, artificial intelligence and Taiwan.The supply line to IranWSJ’s investigation, based on Iranian customs records, US officials and people familiar with the transactions, describes a growing air bridge between China and Iran.Records covering January 2025 through June 2026 show thousands of shipments to Iran's defence ministry and Iranian companies. They included GPS tracking equipment, electric motors and aircraft-engine components. Many shipments carried references to Article 119 of Iranian customs regulations, which provides tariff exemptions for defence imports.The flow intensified after the US Navy restricted Iranian maritime trade.Iranian airline Mahan Air, which is under US sanctions, increased flights from Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou to Tehran from four a week in early March to about 27 a week by late April, according to FlightRadar24 data.By the first week of September, Mahan Air had flown 39 times from China to Iran, roughly twice its prewar level. Many of those flights appeared to be focused on cargo rather than passengers, WSJ reported.Researchers tracking Iranian trade told WSJ that some of the Chinese suppliers involved are little-known companies working with Iranian importers.Kate Koren, deputy director of the economics programme at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told WSJ that some of the components being traded are known to be used in Iran's Shahed drones. A forthcoming CSIS report, she said, identified Chinese companies publicly advertising sensitive electronics this year.The report also stated that Chinese companies have supplied Iran with chemical materials including sodium perchlorate, which can be used to make propellant for ballistic missiles. US authorities have also sanctioned Chinese and Hong Kong-based companies over alleged efforts to help Iran acquire weapons and military equipment.In one case, US officials said a procurement network tried to obtain Chinese shoulder-fired missile systems for Iran and route them through Belarus to conceal the Iranian end-user. The attempted transaction was unsuccessful, according to those officials.China's oil lifeline; and Washington's dilemmaThe relationship is not one-sided but rather symbiotic.China has become Iran's largest oil customer, providing Tehran with a major source of revenue despite US sanctions. Chinese front companies and financial networks have helped facilitate Iranian oil transactions and move money through China's financial system.Iran and China deepened their relationship after the Trump administration's 2018 "maximum pressure" campaign. The two countries signed a 25-year strategic cooperation pact in 2021, while China became the dominant buyer of Iranian crude.US lawmakers have said China buys more than 80% of Iran's crude exports. More recently, a US Senate foreign relations committee statement citing Treasury figures put the share at about 90%.Washington has responded with hundreds of sanctions against Iranian and Chinese entities since the war began, including companies accused of helping Tehran obtain weapons, components or revenue.Yet the Trump administration has so far been cautious about directly confronting Beijing, especially after the earlier tariff confrontation exposed China’s leverage.People familiar with discussions inside the administration told WSj that Trump had made maintaining good relations with Xi a priority ahead of the summit. Some senior officials have consequently played down the significance of Chinese assistance to Iran.That approach has created disagreement within Washington, with defence secretary Pete Hegseth blaming China for enabling Iran, a claim Trump rejected stating, “I trust them.”The satellite trailAccording to US officials cited by WSJ, Iran used satellite imagery obtained from Chinese entities before and after a July 17 strike that killed three US troops.The Trump administration had already sanctioned three Chinese satellite-imagery companies in May, saying the companies had provided information that could help Iran target US forces.That has intensified pressure within Washington to confront Beijing.In late August, Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent launched "Operation Economic Outcast", aimed at cutting the economic networks sustaining Iran. The US subsequently sanctioned a China-owned oil tanker and Chinese companies and individuals accused of helping Iran obtain critical components.But the administration did not impose major new sanctions directly on Chinese financial institutions.Meanwhile, Iranian oil has continued reaching China.Kpler estimated that around four million barrels were delivered to China in the week after Operation Economic Outcast began.And despite sanctions and the wider conflict, Mahan Air continues to fly to China.Contradiction at the heart of the Xi-Trump summitXi’s arrival in Washington now carries two very different messages.China wants to be seen as a country capable of brokering peace and stabilising the Middle East. Beijing has publicly rejected attempts to associate it with the conflict and says it opposes unilateral US sanctions and supports diplomatic efforts to end the fighting.At the same time, WSJ’s investigation found evidence of continued Chinese trade with Iran involving components that can have military applications.Chinese officials have said Beijing strictly regulates exports of dual-use goods and rejects allegations that it is deliberately supporting the conflict.The tension is therefore not simply about whether China supports Iran. It is about how far Beijing is willing to go, and how far Washington is willing to push back, while both sides try to preserve a broader relationship.The same China that Trump wants to keep close for trade and strategic reasons is deeply embedded in the economic and supply networks helping Iran sustain itself.And that makes Iran an awkward third presence at a summit ostensibly about America and China.You use AI every day. articles.title: Amazon settles a class-action case over allegations involving its return policies in Washington; proposes $309.5 million fund for customers: Who is eligible
articles.summary: Amazon has agreed to a proposed $309.5 million settlement fund in a class-action case involving allegations about its return and refund policies in the
articles.body: Amazon has agreed to a proposed $309.5 million settlement fund in a class-action case involving allegations about its return and refund policies in the Washington state. The case concerns customers who may not have received refunds correctly or on time, or who received a refund and were later charged again for returned products. As stated in an AP report, Amazon has denied the allegations and any wrongdoing. The court, on the other hand, has not found that Amazon violated any law or engaged in misconduct.As per the report, the proposed settlement will need court approval. The court has scheduled a Final Approval Hearing for March 16, 2027, at 10 am in Seattle, Washington. If approved, eligible customers could receive payments under the settlement terms.Who is eligible for the Amazon refund settlementThe settlement has two groups, known as Subclass A and Subclass B. The payment process is different for each group. A person may qualify if they:- Initiated a return to Amazon or requested a refund for a physical product purchased through Amazon.com.- Amazon's records show that the product was received in the US.- The purchase and return or refund falls between September 5, 2017, and February 12, 2026.- The customer either did not receive a refund, received a late or incorrect refund, or received a refund but was later charged by Amazon for the returned product.How much money will Amazon payUnder the proposed settlement, Amazon will pay $309.5 million into a non-reversionary common fund. The fund will be used to make payments to eligible class members according to the settlement's distribution plan. It will also cover payments to the settlement administrator and other settlement-related costs, including attorneys' fees and incentive awards, subject to court approval.Amazon also said it identified some potentially unpaid refunds after the lawsuit was filed. In 2025, the company began a process to pay some of those refunds.These included refunds that were not completed because of payment-processing problems and refunds where Amazon did not have enough confirmation that the correct products had been returned.Under the proposed settlement, Amazon has agreed to make reasonable efforts to complete these payments separately from the $309.5 million settlement fund.How can eligible Amazon customers get refundThe process depends on which settlement subclass a customer belongs to. Subclass A members will automatically receive a payment under the settlement. However, they must visit the settlement website within 105 days after the court grants final approval to select their preferred payment method.While the Subclass B members must submit a claim form to receive a payment. Claims must be submitted online or by mail by December 1, 2026.Customers can find the claim form and other settlement information at ReturnSettlement.com.Amazon denies the allegationsThe lawsuit, In re: Amazon Return Policy Litigation, is pending in the US District Court for the Western District of Washington Amazon denies the plaintiffs' allegations and denies any wrongdoing.The court, on the other hand, has not determined that Amazon engaged in misconduct or violated consumer protection laws. The court has also not yet decided whether the case should proceed as a class action. The proposed settlement would resolve the case if it receives final approval.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1952, a French doctor deliberately crossed the Atlantic alone in an inflatable life raft with no provisions; 65 days later, he reached the Caribbean alive and published an account of his voyage
articles.summary: In 1952, French doctor Alain Bombard undertook a perilous journey crossing the Atlantic Ocean in an inflatable life raft without provisions to prove his theories on maritime survival. His incredible story of resilience and innovative survival tactics sheds light on human endurance against the odds.
articles.body: Typically, doctors are trained to protect others from danger, not to put themselves in it. However, in the early 1950s, a French doctor came to believe the only way to prove his theory about maritime survival was to survive it himself, living off only what the sea could provide.Alain Bombard's conviction grew out of a single terrible morning in 1951, when he was a young hospital intern in Boulogne-sur-Mer and was called in urgently after a fishing trawler sank, leaving dozens of the crew dead or injured. Bombard had been unable to save a single one of them, an experience that stayed with him and pushed him to study why so many shipwreck victims died even after reaching a lifeboat or a life raft, an episode later recorded in the French Navy's own account of his life. His research led him to conclude that castaways often died less from the sea itself and more from thirst, despair and a lack of basic knowledge about what the ocean could provide.Bombard determined he would deliberately become a castaway to test his theory. In 1952 he started off in a small inflatable boat called L'Hérétique (French for the heretic) with no food, no fresh water, only a sextant and some modest fishing tackle. He did save a tiny sealed store of emergency supplies, which had been constructed under the notary's seal with the express understanding that he was not to break it open unless his life really depended upon it. That seal was not broken.Small amounts of saltwater, plankton, and fishBombard’s proposal was based on concepts he had formed from studying the nutritional qualities of marine life, suggesting that fish flesh and small amounts of seawater, ingested deliberately rather than in desperation, could support a person for weeks at sea. He caught fish with a harpoon and hooks produced at home, drank the juice of freshly caught fish and added to it plankton captured with a little hand net. He also drank small amounts of seawater during the voyage, a practice widely regarded as harmful at the time and one he hoped to show might be tolerated in small doses.The voyage was far from smooth. On the transatlantic leg, which started on 20 October 1952 from the Canary Islands, Bombard had to patch a ripped sail four days into the leg after his spare was blown away in a storm that momentarily left his boat half submerged. Later a navigation mistake made him believe he was travelling quicker than he was, and on his fifty-third day at sea, he was intercepted by a passing British cargo ship, whose crew told him he still had well over a thousand km to go. They fed him well, a meal he later said gave him the worst indigestion of the whole passage, and a moment where he could have abandoned the effort and gone home but chose not to.Bombard finally reached Barbados on 24 December 1952, 65 days and roughly 6,000 kilometres after leaving the Canaries, and around four months after his research began at the Oceanographic Institute in Monaco earlier that year. He had lost roughly 25 kilograms in weight and needed brief hospital treatment, yet he was able to walk the final stretch to a rescue station under his own strength, a detail that became central to the case he had set out to prove.A legacy over the seaBombard’s expedition made him a public figure. He spent much of the rest of his life pursuing marine research and environmental causes rather than returning to the practice of medicine. In 1966 he helped build a new marine research station on an island off the southern coast of France, which today operates as the Paul Ricard Oceanographic Institute, devoted to the study and preservation of marine environments. Bombard later also entered politics, sitting as a member of the European Parliament for France between 1981 and 1994.Professionals still contest Bombard's methods, and doctors generally do not advise people to consume seawater. Even so, his expedition prompted renewed discussion of what a person adrift at sea might achieve with knowledge and discipline. More than 70 years later, an inflatable survival raft is still sometimes called a “bombard” in French, a small linguistic nod to the doctor who volunteered to be shipwrecked to test his theory.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kristin Cavallari bought a secluded 130-acre Tennessee estate in 2024 and spent two years reshaping it, turning a barn into an indoor basketball court and a guesthouse into her podcast studio
articles.summary: For Kristin Cavallari, the appeal of her new Tennessee home goes well beyond its size.
articles.body: For Kristin Cavallari, the appeal of her new Tennessee home goes well beyond its size. Tucked away on 130 acres outside Nashville, the secluded estate has become a private base for family life, work and the slower pace she wanted after moving on from her former Nashville property. The reality television veteran was not actively house hunting when a real estate agent friend encouraged her to visit the one-story residence in 2024. The combination of privacy, expansive land and floor-to-ceiling windows quickly changed that. What followed was a two-year transformation focused less on dramatic decoration and more on making the property work around her life and her three children, states an online report by Realtor.A new chapter outside NashvilleAs per the report, Cavallari had been looking for a fresh start after selling the Nashville home she had once shared with former NFL quarterback Jay Cutler. The former couple, who split in 2020, finalized their divorce in 2022 and sold their shared mansion for $3.7 million in 2020, considerably below its $5.3 million purchase price in 2012 and its later $7.9 million asking price.Cavallari also purchased another Nashville property for $3 million around the time she and Cutler announced their separation. Her current estate, however, offered something those homes could not: expansive acreage and a much greater degree of privacy, adds the report. She shares the Tennessee property with sons Camden, 14, and Jaxon, 12, and daughter Saylor, 10.A familiar design languageAccording to Architectural Digest, for the interiors, Cavallari again worked with longtime friend and interior designer April Tomlin. The pair had previously created a calm, grounding aesthetic in Cavallari's former home, using neutral tones, bright white interiors and understated furnishings. That visual language carried into the new residence. Surprisingly little needed to be changed, with Cavallari bringing much of her existing furniture into the property. Even many of the home's original details, including its light fixtures, remained. Tomlin's approach centered on a no-fuss environment that could still feel warm and comfortable, with muted and earthy tones providing much of the visual character.Turning the property into a one-stop homeThe Architectural Digest report adds that the biggest transformation was functional. Because of the estate's remote location, Cavallari wanted to reduce the amount of time spent driving back and forth for everyday activities. A home gym eliminated a roughly 25-minute drive each way, while a new bathtub and a substantially larger closet added practical upgrades inside the main house. The expanded closet also became part of the home's design, with Cavallari's clothing collection influencing the space.The barn was converted into an indoor basketball court for her sons, giving the boys a dedicated space to play without leaving the property. The guesthouse took on a professional role, becoming a recording studio for Cavallari's Let's Be Honest podcast, which has secured a seven-figure deal with Dear Media.Creating a quieter retreatThe report adds that a new pool completed the outdoor transformation. Designed by Basin Pool Designs owner Nick Buchholz, the pool was conceived to create a sense of calm while visually connecting with the house rather than feeling like a separate feature. After two years of changes, the estate has evolved into more than a large rural property. Its design, amenities and layout have been carefully shaped around Cavallari's daily routine and her children's interests.The result is a home that combines expansive surroundings with a surprisingly practical approach to family life, giving Cavallari the privacy of a secluded estate without sacrificing the comforts of a house designed for everyday living.Images Courtesy: instagram and Architectural DigestYou use AI every day. articles.title: California shoppers with disabilities say mall skincare stores pressured them into spending thousands; one man says he spent more than $50,000, and a congressman is now seeking state scrutiny
articles.summary: Customers with disabilities and older adults said that they were allegedly pressured into spending thousands of dollars at Bee & Co.'s mall-based skincare
articles.body: Customers with disabilities and older adults said that they were allegedly pressured into spending thousands of dollars at Bee & Co.'s mall-based skincare stores across the Southland, according to CBS California. Now, California congressman Rep. Brad Sherman, whose congressional district includes the Westfield Topanga mall in Canoga Park, said he plans to bring the allegations involving Bee & Co. to the attention of California Attorney General Rob Bonta. "This is not what should be going on in our malls," Sherman said.The investigation developed from a previous story by CBS California Investigates where Victor Chisholm, a man with an intellectual disability, said he spent more than $50,000 during several visits to Bee & Co. last spring. Chisholm told CBS LA that he felt pressured into draining his savings account. When asked if he wanted to spend that amount, Chisholm said, "Uh, no. I did not."Bee & Co. is a skincare and wellness brand that offers natural products and in-store treatments. Since the report about Chisholm was published, other customers have come forward with similar allegations. Gabe Cota, who has a learning disability, said he spent more than $3,000 at Bee & Co. after being drawn into the store by a free sample and a compliment from a saleswoman. "At that point, I was basically in their web, and I couldn't escape until they made a sale," Cota said.Cota said he is slow to process information and that compliments about his appearance can make him feel vulnerable. "Most of my life, I've never really felt attractive," he said. "Part of it is lack of self-confidence." He said the same Bee & Co. salesperson who interacted with Chisholm also persuaded him to make purchases even after he said he did not want to.He said he even locked his debit card to prevent himself from making another purchase but, according to Cota, the salesperson convinced him to send $300 through Zelle. "It makes me angry, it makes me upset, and then it also makes me feel disillusioned because I'm the kind of person who has difficulty saying no to people," Cota said.Chisholm and Cota both alleged that the same salesperson flirted with them and used sales tactics that made them feel pressured to hand over their credit cards.Bee & Co.'s parent company, Mazal Group, is based in Chatsworth. The company recently settled a class-action lawsuit brought by more than 100 customers who alleged unfair and deceptive practices at the company's skincare stores in Hawaii. The customers alleged nearly $1 million in losses.Mazal has denied wrongdoing in connection with the allegations. In a recent email to Chisholm's attorney, Fred Voigtmann, Bee & Co. attorney Efrat Levy said it was Chisholm who engaged in "harassing and inappropriate conduct." Levy also said Bee & Co. "denies any wrongdoing."According to the email, the company offered to return Chisholm's money if he and his attorney removed disparaging comments and online reviews and sent a letter to Westfield stating that Voigtmann "did not know what actually took place between Bee & Co. and its sales representatives and Mr Chisholm."Westfield, which operates the Topanga mall, said in an email that the "reported treatment of this customer is deeply troubling" and that it was "evaluating appropriate legal remedies."According to Sherman, the allegations could create problems for the mall. "This is a reputational risk, perhaps even a legal risk for the mall," he said.The allegations are not limited to Bee & Co. In 2024, a Mazal-affiliated store called Lionesse at Westfield Fashion Square in Sherman Oaks settled a lawsuit with a woman in her 70s who accused the business of elder abuse and deceptive sales practices.Two women, both now in their 80s, also told the station they were pressured into buying expensive skincare products at Mazal-affiliated stores at the Shops at Santa Anita. Both took their cases to small claims court, where they reached settlements. The mall declined to comment, saying the matter involved an "independently operated tenant."Simon, which owns Del Amo Fashion Centre, was also contacted repeatedly for comment but did not respond.The allegations against the retailers have not been adjudicated in court, and the companies have denied wrongdoing in connection with the claims. Chisolm's attorney has created a website where people can report their experiences with coercive skincare sales.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: McDonald's says its AI-enabled drive-thru system can now take orders in English and Spanish with 90% accuracy; it could save at least 50 labour hours a week; CFO Ian Borden notes that company has no intention to reduce staff
articles.summary: McDonald’s announced that its AI-enabled drive-thru system called Archy can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy.
articles.body: McDonald’s announced that its AI-enabled drive-thru system called Archy can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. According to a report by CBS, the company said that the system could save at least 50 labour hours per week at a typical restaurant by streamlining order-taking. CFO Ian Borden also stressed that the intention is not to reduce staff but to free employees to focus on hospitality and food preparation tasks, such as hand-breading chicken.$8.5 billion global modernization plan of McDonald’sThe announcement came as McDonald’s unveiled a $8.5 billion investment plan over the next decade to modernize its 46,000 restaurants worldwide. CEO Chris Kempczinski said the company must improve productivity and capture market share in a flat fast-food traffic environment. Planned upgrades include lockers for delivery orders, redesigned kitchen layouts, bigger play areas, and more visible coffee preparation stations to enhance quality perceptions.Archy and ArchIQ: AI at the center of the planA key piece of the modernization push is McDonald's AI-enabled drive-thru ordering system, Archy, which the company says can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. According to CFO Ian Borden, the system could eventually save at least 50 labor hours per week at a typical restaurant. Importantly, Borden was clear that the goal isn't to cut staffing — instead, employees freed up from order-taking would be redirected toward hospitality-focused tasks or hands-on food preparation work, like hand-breading chicken.Archy operates alongside ArchIQ, a broader AI system McDonald's developed in partnership with Google that's designed to improve order accuracy while automating backend tasks like inventory management and staff scheduling. Kempczinski said early testing shows customers have responded well to Archy specifically because it makes their orders more accurate, adding that the company's approach to AI isn't rooted in treating the technology as inherently good or bad, but in being deliberate about how it's actually deployed.Beyond AI: physical store upgradesThe modernization plan extends well past software. McDonald's said upcoming restaurant redesigns will include lockers for handling delivery orders, more visible coffee preparation areas meant to improve customers' perception of quality, larger play areas, and reworked kitchen layouts. Order-accuracy scales, already active in 10,000 restaurants globally, are set to expand to 20,000 locations by 2028.Menu changes driven by protein demandOn the food side, McDonald's highlighted strong results from its hand-breaded chicken, currently rolled out across 10,000 restaurants in Asia and a small number of locations near Chicago, with plans to expand testing into additional US markets and Ireland next year — a category where rivals like Chick-fil-A and KFC have long had an edge. The company also plans to introduce grilled chicken sandwiches and wraps, along with experimenting with items like egg bites and bowls.Skye Anderson, president of McDonald's USA, tied this shift directly to changing consumer habits, noting that roughly 30 million Americans currently use GLP-1 weight loss drugs and are increasingly seeking smaller, protein-dense meals as a result. She pointed to internal research suggesting a much larger opportunity, though, with roughly 60 million Americans actively looking to add more protein to their diets overall — a gap she framed as a chance for McDonald's to give customers more reasons to choose the brand first.Staying focused on value amid cost-of-living pressureDespite the modernization push, Kempczinski emphasized that value remains central to McDonald's strategy, particularly for lower-income consumers. He defined low-income US households as those earning $45,000 or less annually, noting that while this group still eats fast food, they're doing so less frequently than before. He credited meal bundles like the $5 meal deal with helping address that pressure, and said McDonald's is exploring introducing entry-level pricing on a basic menu of items in the US, mirroring an approach it already uses in Europe and other markets. He described the current economic backdrop as one demanding constant attention to value, noting that cost-of-living pressure on consumers isn't going away anytime soon.Employee training and customer valueMcDonald’s is also rolling out new hospitality-focused training, showing employees what a perfectly cooked Big Mac tastes like and encouraging more pleasant customer interactions. At the same time, the company remains focused on value, exploring entry-level pricing for basic menu items in the U.S. to counter cost-of-living pressures.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2009, a British filmmaker left home to visit 201 countries without a flight; four years later, he had reached them by road, rail and sea
articles.summary: Explore the incredible journey of Graham Hughes, a British filmmaker who traveled to every country in the world using only public transport, raising funds for WaterAid and creating a unique travel narrative.
articles.body: Since a plane can reach almost any capital city in a day or two, the idea of travelling to every country in the world has become almost commonplace for anyone with the means and time. When that option is eliminated, however, the same objective becomes something far more like an expedition than a checklist, complete with malfunctioning buses, cargo ships that sail according to no set schedule, and borders that occasionally refuse to let a passenger pass.Liverpool filmmaker and adventurer Graham Hughes had exactly such a restriction in mind when he set off on 1 January 2009, crossing from Argentina into Uruguay to start what he named the Odyssey Expedition. Hughes, who only travelled by bus, train, taxi, cargo ship and foot, and who would not hitchhike, drive himself or board a single airline, arrived in his 201st and last country, South Sudan, on November 26, 2012, finishing the voyage in four years and 31 days. His achievement was later confirmed by Guinness World Records as the fastest time to visit every country utilising just public surface transit.Crossing seas without ever flyingThe biggest issue was reaching island nations and those separated by open water, since scheduled public transit rarely served them and Hughes had to find what passage he could. On one occasion, he sailed four days across open water in a small wooden boat to reach Cape Verde. Elsewhere, he scheduled his movements around infrequent cargo ships that might only visit a remote port once every few weeks or so. His thorough account of the entire journey, country by country, The Odyssey Expedition, says he spent a week in jail in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was arrested trying to enter Russia and had to run a blockade to get to Cuba.Hughes also recorded and presented a television series on the first 133 countries of his tour, made for Lonely Planet and screened in more than sixty countries by National Geographic and the BBC in eight parts. All of the trip was on a tight budget of around one hundred dollars a week, the money coming mostly from savings, credit and assistance from family and friends, and Hughes was surviving on couchsurfing, cheap hostels and extended stretches of not eating properly so as to keep costs down.A trip with a benevolent purpose attached to itAs well as the record, Hughes also used the journey to raise funds and awareness for WaterAid, an international charity that aims to expand access to clean water, good sanitation and basic hygiene in communities throughout the world. The link was made obvious by how often Hughes found himself reliant on the kindness and basic infrastructure of the countries he passed through, from a surprise meeting with the Prime Minister of Tuvalu to nights spent in villages where he was the only stranger for miles.The subsequent verification of its completion was almost as taxing as the journey itself. The record was officially certified by Guinness World Records in 2014 after more than a year spent examining over a million GPS data points, ten thousand photographs, four hundred hours of video, and every page of Hughes’s passports; in part because Hughes had to return to Russia in January 2013, after the expedition itself had ended, to correct an earlier illegal border crossing there.What the narrative ultimately shows is less about travel bragging rights and more about what becomes possible when plane travel is deliberately excluded. In each of the 201 nations Hughes visited, he was obliged to rely only on scheduled ground and sea transport, which meant direct interaction with ordinary people and unglamorous logistics, a slower and considerably more grounded way of seeing the world than most travelers ever attempted.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Global system is failing to addess crisis', says Rubio citing ‘potential conflict’ between India, Pakistan
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday cited a “potential conflict between India and Pakistan” as an example of the international system’s
articles.body: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday cited a “potential conflict between India and Pakistan” as an example of the international system’s inability to address major conflicts and crises, saying there was currently no “functional” global system capable of dealing with such situations.Addressing a press conference in New York, Rubio said the international system was “not in good shape” and pointed to several conflicts and tensions around the world, including the Thailand-Cambodia conflict, the situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, Sudan and Iran in the straits.“The international system is not in good shape right now... it would be great if we had a functional international system, for example, that could deal with a war between Thailand and Cambodia that occurred or the potential conflict between India and Pakistan,” Rubio said.“Right now, we don't seem to have a functional international system that can address it. And in the absence of that, nation-states will act in their national interest,” he said.Rubio also made clear that Washington would continue to prioritise US interests, saying, “We will never put the international order above the interest of the United States.”Flags India-Pakistan tensionsRubio’s remarks come against the backdrop of India and Pakistan’s military hostilities in 2025 following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people were killed.India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7 in response to the attack, targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. Following Indian strikes on terror launchpads, military action between the two countries was paused on May 10 after Pakistan approached India for cessation of hostilities.US President Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed credit for stopping the India-Pakistan fighting and has said his administration helped broker an understanding between the two sides.India, however, has consistently rejected any suggestion of third-party mediation, maintaining that the cessation of military action was reached directly between India and Pakistan through their respective military channels.Rubio said several world leaders had also raised concerns about the current international framework, arguing that it had expanded beyond its original purpose and was failing to resolve major conflicts.“I think multiple leaders... pointed to the fact that the international system is failing, and it's failing because it has grown beyond its mandate. It has grown beyond its intent,” Rubio said.He alleged that the system had become involved in areas beyond its intended role while remaining unable to resolve major conflicts.You use AI every day.
